Solomon Islands signs treaty with Australia that checks China's influence in the South Pacific
articles.description: Solomon Islands signs treaty with Australia that checks China's influence in the South Pacific AP News China’s Military Ambitions in the Pacific Suffer Setback WSJ Solomon Islands plans to replace China security pact with Australia treaty, report says Reuters Solomon Islands ends controversial security pact with China for Australian treaty BBC This nation had a security pact with China. It’s just signed a deal with a
articles.content: MELBOURNE, Australia (AP) — The Solomon Islands rejected a secretive 4-year-old defense deal with China that raised fears of a Chinese naval foothold in the South Pacific country and declared Wednesday while signing a treaty with Australia that it would never allow a foreign military base on its soil. The Solomons’ archipelago is sprawled across the sea route between the United States and Australia, from where U.S. Gen. Douglas MacArthur commanded the Pacific campaign in World War II. U.S. allies fought pivotal battles against Japanese forces on the islands during the war, and the country that today has a population of fewer than 900,000 people remains strategically imperative territory in the U.S. struggle against China for global influence. The islands’ Prime Minister Matthew Wale and his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese signed the bilateral security pact following reports that the Solomons will end its defense treaty with China next year. The new treaty confirms Australia’s place as the Solomons’ “primary security partner” and states “there will be no foreign military or security base” on the smaller nation 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) northeast of Australia, both prime ministers said in a statement. The deal is the latest bilateral security pact Australia has struck with Pacific neighbors since Beijing inked a treaty with the Solomons’ previous government in 2022 that created fears the Chinese navy would build a base in the South Pacific. Since Albanese’s government was first elected in late 2022, Australia, a staunch U.S. ally, has been attempting to edge Chinese influence out of the region through bilateral security agreements with countries including Fiji, Tuvalu and Vanuatu. Australia reached a security-linked pact with Papua New Guinea in 2024 that promised Australia’s nearest neighbor 600 million Australian dollars ($396 million) over a decade to include a rugby league team in the Australian national competition. Wale would not confirm or deny news media reports that his government had told Beijing that the security pact with China, which has provided Chinese police trainers to the Solomons’ capital Honiara, would not be renewed when it expires after five years in early 2027. “Unfortunately there is a non-disclosure clause in the treaty with China,” Wale told reporters in a press conference with Albanese at Australian Parliament House. “So I am unable to talk about that. We have ongoing discussions with China.” “As you know, Solomon Islands has been, for a number of years, a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done. Gone. We don’t want to be there again,” he added. In Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun did not directly answer a journalist’s question about whether the Solomons had said it would end the Chinese security pact. “China always follows the principle of mutual respect and equality in developing relations with the Solomon Islands,” Guo said Tuesday. “There is no element of geopolitical rivalry or bloc confrontation in cooperation between China and Pacific island countries, including the Solomon Islands.” Albanese said the new bilateral treaty elevated bilateral relations to a “level which has never been seen before and has never been stronger.” The treaty is broader than security. Australia has agreed to also invest in Solomons’ infrastructure, education, renewable energy and sport. Oliver Nobetau, Pacific Islands program director at the Lowy Institute, a Sydney think tank, described the treaty as significant and fine-tuned to the Solomons’ priorities. “It demonstrates that Australia is listening to what the Pacific partners want,” Nobetau told Australian Broadcasting Corp.

Golden Harvest is the gold standard for breakfast
articles.description: When you’ve just boiled two eggs for breakfast on a Sunday morning and your friend texts you, “Golden Harvest?” you forget everything you said earlier in the week about eating […]
articles.content: When you’ve just boiled two eggs for breakfast on a Sunday morning and your friend texts you, “Golden Harvest?” you forget everything you said earlier in the week about eating out less. Life is short but also tedious, so — for me, anyway — it’s impossible to resist the zest that a tasty meal with a friend can add to life for the sake of things like “practicality” and “a budget.” Thankfully, Golden Harvest’s flat rate of $15 per breakfast won’t break the bank. However, deciding what to get is always a struggle. On my last visit, the restaurant had even more options up on its whiteboards than usual, further complicating things. My friend wanted — and offered to share — the Killer Quesadilla, which I had already planned on ordering after seeing a tantalizing photo of it on Facebook, so I got myself the home fries deluxe plate. Home fries deluxe. Lizy Ferguson for City Pulse Despite being amiably teased by our waiter for ordering something boring, this dish was anything but. A perfectly cooked and seasoned mountain of diced red potatoes was topped with lightly wilted spinach, onions, peppers, mushrooms, feta cheese, two of the most beautiful sunny-side-up eggs I’ve ever seen, and a rich and luscious garlic aioli. Every bite of this was so good, I kept putting my fork down and shaking my head in disbelief, wondering why I had ever eaten breakfast anywhere else. Home fries deluxe and how to get ’em $15 Golden Harvest 1625 Turner St., Lansing 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Thursday-Sunday facebook.com/goldenharvestrestaurant And then there was the quesadilla, another masterpiece. Fluffy scrambled eggs and melty cheddar cheese were wrapped in a crispy tortilla, accompanied by perfectly ripe avocado, sour cream and homemade salsa that was out of this world. Because the portions are enormous, we both had to get boxes for our leftovers. Mine made for a perfect lunch when I was finally hungry again, many hours later. People often mention the wait time at Golden Harvest, but it’s more than justified when you receive your plate. They refuse to rush in order to deliver a fast but subpar meal, which is a hard impulse to resist and deserves the utmost respect. The proof is in the pudding — specifically the banana pudding French toast, which I’ve got to try at some point soon.
